question: During a cholera outbreak, stagnant floodwater contaminating a community well represents which part of the epidemiological triangle?

options.A: Host
options.B: Agent
options.C: Environment
options.D: Immunity

explanation: Well done! The contaminated water is part of the environment—the external surrounding that allows the germ to reach people. You're mastering the basics! [learn more](GNS214_U1_T77#GNS214_U1_T77_h2)

question: What is the main goal of pharmacovigilance?

options.A: Accelerating the clinical trial phase for vaccines
options.B: Calculating the manufacturing costs of new medicines
options.C: Monitoring and preventing drug-related adverse effects
options.D: Determining the patent length for pharmaceutical drugs

explanation: You've got this! Pharmacovigilance is simply the science of watching out for, checking, and stopping bad drug reactions before they harm patients. [learn more](GNS215_U2_T1#GNS215_U2_T1_h1)

question: What three things make up the surgical fire triangle?

options.A: Heat, light, and pressure
options.B: Ignition source, oxidizer, and fuel
options.C: Anesthetic gas, patient, and surgeon
options.D: Electricity, water, and metal

explanation: Correct! A fire needs a spark (ignition), oxygen (oxidizer), and something to burn (fuel) to start in the theatre. [learn more](GNS123_U5_T1#GNS123_U5_T1_h6)

question: Why should you always call the receiving hospital before transferring a patient?

options.A: To ask the receiving hospital for permission to discharge the patient home
options.B: To ensure the receiving team is prepared and has the necessary bed and staff ready
options.C: To negotiate the cost of fuel for the transport vehicle
options.D: To verify if the patient has paid their hospital registration fees

explanation: A quick call ahead ensures the team is waiting with a bed and ready to take over critical care without wasting a second. [learn more](GNS321_U2_T13#GNS321_U2_T13_h6)

question: Why is bone weakened enough to cause a pathological fracture in a patient with chronic osteomyelitis?

options.A: The infection turns all the solid bone into liquid fat deposits
options.B: Antibiotic medications dissolve the calcium inside the bone matrix
options.C: Muscles pull so hard on the bone that they snap it in half
options.D: Extensive areas of bone death and destruction compromise the structural integrity

explanation: Areas of necrotic bone and chronic destruction weaken the overall structural framework of the bone, making it prone to breaking under normal stress. [learn more](GNS222_U1_T17#GNS222_U1_T17_h10)

question: A patient comes to the clinic complaining of severe anal pain and bright red blood after passing stool. What test will the doctor likely do first?

options.A: Upper endoscopy
options.B: Barium swallow
options.C: Proctoscopy
options.D: Liver biopsy

explanation: Well done! When symptoms happen right at the end of the digestive tract, a proctoscopy is the quickest and most direct way to see what's going on. [learn more](GNS221_U2_T7#GNS221_U2_T7_h2)

question: What is the primary purpose of a gastrostomy feeding tube?

options.A: To deliver nutrition directly into the stomach
options.B: To provide continuous intravenous hydration
options.C: To bypass the small intestine during digestion
options.D: To remove excess air and fluid from the bowel

explanation: A gastrostomy tube places food and fluids straight into the stomach, bypassing the mouth and esophagus for patients who cannot swallow safely. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T4#GNS212_U1_T4_h1)

question: What acid-base imbalance can develop from continuous stomach suctioning?

options.A: Metabolic acidosis
options.B: Respiratory acidosis
options.C: Metabolic alkalosis
options.D: Respiratory alkalosis

explanation: Sucking out large amounts of acidic stomach fluid leaves the body with excess base, leading to metabolic alkalosis. You're mastering body chemistry! [learn more](GNS213_U3_T3#GNS213_U3_T3_h8)

question: How does the delayed maturation of the prefrontal cortex affect teenage decision-making regarding sex?

options.A: It makes it harder for teens to pause and think through the long-term risks of their actions
options.B: It prevents teenagers from feeling any physical attraction to others
options.C: It causes complete memory loss of safe sex education
options.D: It eliminates all emotional responses to relationships

explanation: Because the prefrontal cortex is still developing, teenagers struggle with impulse control and evaluating future dangers, making impulsive sexual choices more likely. [learn more](GNS312_U3_T9#GNS312_U3_T9_h2)

question: How does fluid in the chest cavity (pleural effusion) make it hard to breathe?

options.A: Fluid enters the alveoli and destroys the natural surfactant
options.B: It blocks the main windpipe and chugs off air supply
options.C: Fluid physically presses against the lung, stopping it from expanding fully
options.D: It forces the heart to beat too fast, causing sudden shock

explanation: You got it! The fluid takes up space in the chest and squeezes the lung from the outside, so it can't puff up nicely when breathing in. [learn more](GNS213_U2_T12#GNS213_U2_T12_h4)

question: What is the best sign that an intersectoral health program is truly sustainable?

options.A: The federal government takes over all local day-to-day management
options.B: The community takes ownership and maintains the project after external support ends
options.C: Foreign donors continue funding the program for at least twenty years
options.D: The local clinic stops seeing patients and focuses only on administrative reports

explanation: Well done! True sustainability means the community is strong enough to keep things running locally all by themselves. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T25#GNS225_U2_T25_h7)

question: What is the most common trigger for a breakthrough seizure in someone with epilepsy?

options.A: Drinking cold water
options.B: Eating too much sugar
options.C: Walking outside in bright sunlight
options.D: Missing prescribed medication doses

explanation: Consistency is key! Skipping meds lets the drug levels drop in the blood, making a seizure much more likely to happen. Remind your patients how important their schedule is. [learn more](GNS222_U4_T11#GNS222_U4_T11_h4)

question: In Nigeria, what traditional support system has historically cared for most older adults?

options.A: International charity organizations
options.B: The extended family system
options.C: Government-run nursing homes
options.D: Private health insurance agencies

explanation: You've got it! Culturally, our extended family network in Nigeria takes the lead in housing and looking after our aging relatives. [learn more](GNS321_U3_T4#GNS321_U3_T4_h7)

question: Why might a patient with poorly controlled diabetes have sugar (glucose) in their urine?

options.A: Kidney tubules stop functioning entirely due to excess insulin
options.B: High urinary pH converts normal proteins into simple sugar molecules
options.C: Blood sugar is so high it overwhelms kidney reabsorption capacity
options.D: The pancreas secretes extra glucose directly into the bladder

explanation: Normally, the kidneys rescue and reabsorb all the sugar. But when blood sugar is super high, the little kidney tubules get overworked and the extra sugar spills over into the urine! [learn more](GNS123_U2_T6#GNS123_U2_T6_h3)

question: How do strict cultural and religious beliefs usually impact a young woman facing an unintended pregnancy?

options.A: They eliminate the need for any form of healthcare
options.B: They automatically provide financial support for single mothers
options.C: They increase the social pressure to carry the pregnancy to term
options.D: They encourage open dialogue between family members

explanation: Correct! Society's strict expectations can make a woman feel like she has zero room to choose otherwise. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T022#GNS226_U5_T022_h3)

question: Why must oxygen delivery tubing be moved away before delivering a shock?

options.A: To keep the plastic tubing from melting onto the chest skin
options.B: To allow space for placing the defibrillator pads correctly
options.C: To stop the patient from breathing too much room air
options.D: To prevent electrical sparks from igniting an oxygen-rich fire

explanation: Oxygen feeds fire! Combining an electrical spark from a defibrillator pad with a high concentration of oxygen right near the chest is a major fire hazard. [learn more](GNS213_U1_T17#GNS213_U1_T17_h4)

question: What is a key nursing responsibility regarding drug distribution?

options.A: Calculating the exact molecular weight of every pill
options.B: Surgically placing IV lines directly into brain tissue
options.C: Synthesizing new chemical formulas in the ward
options.D: Monitoring for unexpected side effects from altered drug binding or blood flow

explanation: As a nurse, you are the safety net! Watching how your patient responds and checking their labs helps you catch any drug distribution issues early on. [learn more](GNS125_U5_T2#GNS125_U5_T2_h8)

question: When should a nurse manager consider revising an existing objective?

options.A: Only when ordered by hospital accountants at the end of the year.
options.B: As soon as the first week of the planning cycle has passed.
options.C: Whenever staff members complain that the work is slightly difficult.
options.D: When unexpected events like a staff shortage or outbreak change clinical conditions.

explanation: Life in a clinic can be unpredictable. When things like sudden outbreaks or staff shortages happen, our plans need to be flexible enough to adapt. [learn more](GST321_U2_T1#GST321_U2_T1_h7)

question: Why is drying the newborn baby immediately after birth a critical nursing action?

options.A: To stimulate the baby to learn how to walk
options.B: To remove the vernix completely so the skin breathes
options.C: To check for hidden birthmarks and bruises
options.D: To prevent heat loss and hypothermia

explanation: Wet skin combined with room air causes rapid evaporation and heat loss, which can lead to dangerous cold stress in newborns. [learn more](GNS324_U3_T15#GNS324_U3_T15_h3)

question: What physical signs are most typical of an acute gout flare in a joint?

options.A: Slow, painless swelling that develops over several months
options.B: Intense redness, extreme tenderness, and localized heat
options.C: Visible shortening of the limb and muscle atrophy
options.D: Cool, pale skin with complete numbness and no pain

explanation: When gout flares up, the joint gets super angry—it turns bright red, feels very hot to the touch, and hurts so much you can barely let anyone look at it. [learn more](GNS222_U1_T15#GNS222_U1_T15_h5)

question: Which of the following is a WRONG practice when using chemical safety gloves?

options.A: Wearing the exact same pair of gloves indefinitely without checking them
options.B: Inspecting the glove material for tears before starting work
options.C: Washing hands thoroughly after safely removing the gloves
options.D: Choosing glove material resistant to the specific chemical used

explanation: Well reasoned! Gloves wear out, tear, and let chemicals soak through over time. You must check them often and replace them regularly—never wear the same pair forever! [learn more](GNS215_U5_T8#GNS215_U5_T8_h5)

question: What hormonal change helps the digestive tract get back to normal after childbirth?

options.A: A rapid drop in progesterone levels
options.B: A continuous high output of estrogen
options.C: A gradual increase in resting cortisol
options.D: A sudden surge in human placental lactogen

explanation: Once the placenta is delivered, progesterone levels drop fast, allowing the digestive tract to bounce right back to its normal tone. [learn more](GNS121_U7_T4#GNS121_U7_T4_h7)

question: Oh no! A patient's chest tube accidentally slips completely out of the chest. What should you grab and apply right away?

options.A: A firm rubber clamp directly across the wound
options.B: An open, dry gauze pad held lightly by hand
options.C: A sterile petroleum gauze taped on three sides
options.D: A tight, four-sided airtight adhesive plaster

explanation: You've got this! Taping a petroleum dressing on three sides lets trapped air escape when they breathe out, but seals shut when they breathe in. [learn more](GNS221_U2_T18#GNS221_U2_T18_h6)

question: Why is an embryo extra sensitive to harmful substances during the first trimester?

options.A: The mother's immune system attacks foreign embryonic cells
options.B: The placenta has not yet absorbed any maternal antibodies
options.C: Major internal organs are actively forming and organizing
options.D: Amniotic fluid volume is too low to cushion the tissues

explanation: Spot on! Because body tissues and organs are forming rapidly during this time (organogenesis), any harmful substance can easily disrupt their normal structure. You are doing great! [learn more](GNS226_U2_T005#GNS226_U2_T005_h2)

question: Within a hospital, who should nurses typically submit completed NAFDAC Yellow Forms to?

options.A: The pharmaceutical manufacturing company's marketing department
options.B: The local police station for criminal investigation
options.C: The patient's family members for safe keeping
options.D: The hospital pharmacovigilance coordinator or designated channel

explanation: Every facility usually has a designated person or office responsible for gathering these forms and forwarding them securely to NAFDAC. [learn more](GNS215_U2_T6#GNS215_U2_T6_h7)

question: Why must you perform hand hygiene immediately after taking off your gloves?

options.A: Hospital policy requires washing hands twice per hour
options.B: Gloves make your hands smell unpleasant
options.C: Microorganisms may have transferred to your skin during removal
options.D: It helps the skin dry out after sweating inside rubber

explanation: Even with careful removal, tiny tears or contact with the outside of gloves can transfer germs to your hands. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T16#GNS122_U2_T16_h5)

question: What is a major cause of faecal incontinence among women in many resource-limited settings?

options.A: Obstetric trauma during childbirth
options.B: Weakness of the upper arm muscles
options.C: Excessive daily consumption of citrus fruits
options.D: Chronic overuse of inhaled medications

explanation: Difficult deliveries with untreated or poorly repaired perineal tears are a leading cause of sphincter damage and subsequent incontinence in women. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T8#GNS212_U1_T8_h3)

question: Which quick bedside test must you do immediately for any unconscious patient?

options.A: Electroencephalogram
options.B: Blood glucose test
options.C: Complete blood count
options.D: Chest X-ray examination

explanation: Always check the sugar first! Low blood sugar can mimic a major stroke or brain injury, and it's super easy to test and fix right at the bedside. [learn more](GNS123_U3_T9#GNS123_U3_T9_h6)

question: Why must a nurse position a patient upright before giving oral medications?

options.A: It speeds up the first-pass metabolism in the liver
options.B: It allows the nurse to check the pulse more easily
options.C: Gravity helps the medication go down safely and prevents choking
options.D: It stops the stomach acid from rising into the throat

explanation: Sitting at a 90-degree angle uses gravity to guide the pill into the esophagus and protects the airway from accidental aspiration. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T14#GNS122_U1_T14_h2)

question: Why is checking a patient's medications a key part of preventing falls?

options.A: Medications are the only known cause of falls in the elderly
options.B: Pharmacists require routine checks to maintain their licenses
options.C: Older adults always take too many vitamins instead of real food
options.D: Many common drugs cause dizziness, sedation, or balance issues

explanation: Spot on! Blood pressure pills and sleeping meds can make a patient dizzy or lightheaded, leading to accidental falls. [learn more](GNS321_U3_T6#GNS321_U3_T6_h4)

question: Why is emotional and psychological support so important during reproductive workups?

options.A: Procedures often involve sensitive body parts and fears about fertility or disease
options.B: Anxiety prevents the laboratory from processing blood samples accurately
options.C: Patients are legally required to attend counseling before any pelvic exam
options.D: Physical pain cannot be managed with medication if the patient is stressed

explanation: Spot on. Reproductive organs carry deep emotional meaning, so it is totally normal for patients to feel anxious, embarrassed, or scared. Your warm support means everything! [learn more](GNS311_U1_T5#GNS311_U1_T5_h2)

question: How should you apply antiseptic skin prep solution to a patient's surgical site?

options.A: In a random zig-zag pattern across the entire torso and limbs
options.B: Starting at the incision site and moving outward in circles
options.C: Starting at the outer edges and scrubbing inward to the center
options.D: Using a back-and-forth motion right over the planned incision

explanation: Always move from clean to dirty! Starting at the incision and working outward ensures you don't drag skin bacteria into the clean cut. [learn more](GNS123_U5_T4#GNS123_U5_T4_h6)

question: What is the main goal of the intensive phase of TB treatment?

options.A: To test if the patient is allergic to all four drugs
options.B: To rapidly reduce the bacterial load and stop infectiousness
options.C: To rebuild the damaged lung tissue back to normal
options.D: To completely finish the entire course of treatment

explanation: Hitting TB hard with four drugs quickly drops the germ count so the patient stops spreading it to others. Excellent clinical milestone! [learn more](GNS223_U2_T6#GNS223_U2_T6_h4)

question: What base material is commonly used in traditional solid rectal suppositories?

options.A: Cooking oil
options.B: Cocoa butter
options.C: Cornstarch paste
options.D: Distilled water

explanation: Cocoa butter is a solid at room temperature but melts easily at normal body temperature, releasing the medicine. [learn more](GNS125_U3_T18#GNS125_U3_T18_h3)

question: What is the main reason for adding pressure support to a patient who is already breathing on their own through a ventilator?

options.A: To paralyze the respiratory muscles during painful procedures
options.B: To help overcome the resistance of the artificial airway
options.C: To completely take over the work of breathing for the patient
options.D: To measure the exact lung compliance of the patient

explanation: Breathing through a narrow plastic tube is tough work! Pressure support gives a gentle push to make it easier for the patient to draw air through the tube. [learn more](GNS213_U2_T18#GNS213_U2_T18_h2)

question: Which of these is a major barrier to healthcare access in rural Nigerian communities?

options.A: Severe shortage of health facilities and poor road networks
options.B: Instant availability of advanced surgical equipment
options.C: Too many well-trained medical doctors per capita
options.D: Excessive number of specialized tertiary hospitals

explanation: Correct! Bad roads and faraway clinics make getting to a hospital a massive challenge for rural villagers. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T022#GNS226_U5_T022_h7)

question: What is the primary goal of teaching oncology patients about emergency warning signs?

options.A: To ensure they seek help quickly before symptoms become life-threatening
options.B: To prevent them from ever experiencing another tumor recurrence
options.C: To train them to manage medical emergencies at home without calling a doctor
options.D: To reduce the financial cost of hospital stays

explanation: Early reporting of red-flag symptoms allows healthcare teams to intervene swiftly before minor issues become full-blown emergencies. [learn more](GNS321_U1_T13#GNS321_U1_T13_h7)

question: Which medication is a go-to choice for treating both bacterial vaginosis and trichomoniasis?

options.A: Fluconazole
options.B: Clotrimazole
options.C: Metronidazole
options.D: Acyclovir

explanation: Metronidazole is a fantastic workhorse antibiotic and anti-parasitic agent that handles both of these conditions wonderfully. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T10#GNS216_U5_T10_h6)

question: A patient says they feel completely full after eating just two spoonfuls of porridge. What is likely happening?

options.A: Rapid healing of the stomach lining
options.B: An allergic reaction to the specific ingredients
options.C: A sudden surge in physical metabolism
options.D: Early satiety caused by slowed digestive function

explanation: Exactly! When digestion slows down in advanced illness, the stomach fills up extremely fast—a concept we call 'early satiety'. [learn more](GNS321_U4_T17#GNS321_U4_T17_h2)

question: Which of these common chest tube practices is actually dangerous and should be avoided?

options.A: Checking breath sounds and respiratory status every four hours
options.B: Clamping the chest tube continuously for routine nursing tasks
options.C: Taping all tubing connections securely to prevent air leaks
options.D: Keeping the drainage system upright and below chest level

explanation: Great clinical thinking! Never clamp a chest tube routinely; it traps air and fluid inside, which can quickly turn into a life-threatening tension pneumothorax. [learn more](GNS221_U2_T18#GNS221_U2_T18_h5)

question: What is usually at the root of organizational conflict?

options.A: Patients refusing to take medication
options.B: A nurse having low self-esteem
options.C: Systemic issues and structural policies
options.D: Personal dislikes between two nurses

explanation: Organizational conflict stems from institutional rules, budgets, and structures rather than personal beefs. [learn more](GST321_U5_T3#GST321_U5_T3_h5)

question: What is the primary mechanism of an autoclave in waste treatment?

options.A: Dissolving metal instruments in strong acids
options.B: Burning waste at extremely high open flames
options.C: Freezing biological specimens to sub-zero temperatures
options.D: Steam sterilization under high pressure

explanation: Autoclaves use pressurized steam to kill all infectious agents present in medical waste effectively. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T15#GNS122_U3_T15_h5)

question: Why might a patient with a weak immune system show very little fever or swelling when they have an infection?

options.A: Their body temperature naturally stays higher than normal limits
options.B: They have fewer white blood cells to trigger the normal inflammatory response
options.C: They produce too many antibodies for local inflammation to occur
options.D: Their blood vessels are permanently dilated and cannot leak fluid

explanation: Fever and swelling are driven by white blood cells sounding the alarm. If a patient's white blood cell count is very low, they lack the troops needed to put up a loud, visible inflammatory fight. [learn more](GNS111_U2_T14#GNS111_U2_T14_h8)

question: During a Visual Inspection with Acetic Acid (VIA) screening for cervical pre-cancer, what liquid is applied to the cervix?

options.A: Iodine tincture
options.B: Vinegar
options.C: Hydrogen peroxide
options.D: Normal saline

explanation: Acetic acid is simply the active ingredient in vinegar! It makes abnormal cells temporarily turn white so the nurse can spot them easily. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T15#GNS214_U1_T15_h5)

question: What is the main job of the glomerulus when making urine?

options.A: Reabsorbing essential glucose back into the bloodstream
options.B: Filtering water and small molecules from the blood
options.C: Secreting excess potassium directly into the tubules
options.D: Storing urine until it is ready for elimination

explanation: Think of the glomerulus like a high-pressure sieve! It pushes fluid and small waste products out of the blood and into the nephron so your body can start making urine. You've got this! [learn more](GNS123_U2_T6#GNS123_U2_T6_h1)

question: Why is it dangerous to rely 100% on a machine monitor without doing a physical check on your patient?

options.A: It prevents the nurse from writing notes in the electronic health record system
options.B: The hospital will charge the patient extra fees for electronic monitoring services
options.C: It always causes the patient to develop severe anxiety and panic attacks
options.D: The machine might malfunction or display data that does not match the patient's actual condition

explanation: You got it! Machines can glitch or give false readings. Your eyes, hands, and clinical judgment as a nurse are always the best safeguard. [learn more](GNS312_U5_T7#GNS312_U5_T7_h5)

question: What is the main action the male partner must take during the withdrawal method?

options.A: Taking an oral herbal tea before sexual activity
options.B: Washing the genital area immediately after intercourse
options.C: Pulling the penis out of the vagina before ejaculation
options.D: Wearing a thin latex sheath throughout intercourse

explanation: Withdrawal is all about timing: the man must remove his penis from the vaginal canal completely before releasing any semen. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T009#GNS226_U6_T009_h4)

question: What routine self-care practice is strongly emphasized to patients at risk for infective endocarditis to prevent bacteria from entering the bloodstream?

options.A: Refusing all routine vaccinations at local health clinics
options.B: Drinking large quantities of palm wine daily
options.C: Maintaining good oral hygiene and regular dental check-ups
options.D: Avoiding all physical exercise for the rest of their lives

explanation: Oral bacteria can easily enter the bloodstream during dental procedures or daily hygiene, making dental care a primary prevention target for endocarditis. [learn more](GNS213_U1_T7#GNS213_U1_T7_h8)

question: What type of bowel prep is usually given right before a proctoscopy?

options.A: A 4-liter gallon prep
options.B: Total fasting for 48 hours
options.C: A cleansing enema
options.D: Oral magnesium citrate

explanation: Spot on! Because a proctoscopy only looks at the very end of the bowel, a quick cleansing enema just before the test is usually all it takes to clear the area. [learn more](GNS221_U2_T7#GNS221_U2_T7_h4)

question: Which of these is NOT a common long-term problem linked to severe perineal trauma?

options.A: Dyspareunia during intercourse
options.B: Gestational diabetes mellitus
options.C: Incontinence of gas or stool
options.D: Chronic pelvic floor pain

explanation: Gestational diabetes is about blood sugar and pregnancy hormones, not physical trauma to the perineum during birth. [learn more](GNS226_U4_T011#GNS226_U4_T011_h7)

question: Why do intramuscular injections get absorbed faster than subcutaneous ones?

options.A: Subcutaneous fat contains no blood vessels
options.B: Muscles produce enzymes that break down drugs
options.C: The needle used is always much thinner
options.D: Muscle tissue has a rich blood supply

explanation: Great job thinking about how drugs move in the body! Muscles have plenty of blood vessels, which helps medications rush quickly into the bloodstream. You've got this! [learn more](GNS122_U1_T3#GNS122_U1_T3_h1)

question: What is the main job of the thalamus (medial geniculate nucleus) along the auditory pathway?

options.A: It produces the endolymph fluid found in the scala media
options.B: It acts as a relay and sorting station before sending signals to the cortex
options.C: It equalizes the fluid pressure between the middle and inner ear
options.D: It directly bends the stereocilia to create neurotransmitters

explanation: The thalamus is like the brain's central bus station—it takes sensory signals, organizes them, and routes them to the right part of the cortex. [learn more](GNS211_U4_T7#GNS211_U4_T7_h6)

question: Which of these is considered a direct cause of maternal death?

options.A: Sickle cell anemia
options.B: Eclampsia
options.C: Severe malaria
options.D: Rheumatic heart disease

explanation: Eclampsia (severe pregnancy-induced high blood pressure leading to seizures) is a direct complication of pregnancy. The others are medical conditions made worse by pregnancy (indirect). [learn more](GNS226_U1_T012#GNS226_U1_T012_h3)

question: What is the primary clinical complication caused by the poliovirus?

options.A: Irreversible muscle paralysis in the limbs
options.B: High fever accompanied by a widespread skin rash
options.C: Uncontrollable fits of violent coughing
options.D: Severe chronic diarrhea and rapid dehydration

explanation: Poliovirus attacks the nervous system, which can lead to total, permanent paralysis, most commonly affecting the legs. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T61#GNS214_U1_T61_h4)

question: Why must patients with liver disease avoid taking casual painkillers like paracetamol without asking a doctor?

options.A: It neutralizes the effects of prescribed lactulose syrup
options.B: The liver has to process it, and it can cause more damage
options.C: It causes severe allergic skin rashes in liver patients
options.D: It increases the risk of dehydration and kidney failure

explanation: Medications like paracetamol are processed by the liver. When the liver is weak, these drugs can build up quickly and cause serious harm. [learn more](GNS222_U2_T5#GNS222_U2_T5_h7)

question: A patient with severe malaria is admitted to your ward. How should they first receive their medication?

options.A: Oral tablets swallowed with water
options.B: Subcutaneous daily injection
options.C: Rectal suppositories only
options.D: Intravenous or intramuscular

explanation: Well done! Severe cases move fast, so we need fast-acting injections (IV or IM artesunate) to get the drug into their system immediately. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T3#GNS214_U1_T3_h5)

question: A patient needs a very early pregnancy test using urine. Which sample should you tell her to collect?

options.A: First morning urine
options.B: Timed two-hour urine
options.C: Random afternoon urine
options.D: Post-exercise urine

explanation: First morning urine is the most concentrated, meaning any early pregnancy hormones will be nice and strong and easy for the test to pick up! [learn more](GNS123_U2_T6#GNS123_U2_T6_h2)

question: An older stroke patient says their biggest goal is to walk to the backyard garden to see flowers. How should you use this?

options.A: Ignore the statement because garden visits are not medical milestones
options.B: Tell the patient to pick a standard treadmill speed instead
options.C: Incorporate the garden walk into realistic, patient-centered goal setting
options.D: Discharge the patient immediately since they have outdoor desires

explanation: You've got this! When rehab goals matter personally to the patient, they feel much more motivated to work hard and get better. [learn more](GNS321_U3_T6#GNS321_U3_T6_h2)

question: A patient with terminal cancer is unable to speak but is frowning, restless, and breathing rapidly. What should the nurse suspect?

options.A: The patient is fully relaxed and ready for sleep
options.B: The patient is recovering normal neurological function
options.C: The patient is having an allergic reaction to food

options.C: Monitors are generally illegal to use without a physician present
options.D: Monitors only measure body temperature and nothing else

explanation: Machines are great helpers, but they aren't human! A simple movement can mess up the reading. Always double-check the monitor numbers by actually looking at and touching your patient. [learn more](GNS321_U2_T8#GNS321_U2_T8_h2)

question: Which of these is a key nursing check during routine postnatal care?

options.A: Surgically repairing minor perineal tears after 6 weeks
options.B: Administering the BCG vaccine to the mother
options.C: Measuring the child's head circumference daily
options.D: Checking uterine involution and lochia flow

explanation: Well done! Monitoring how the uterus shrinks (involution) and the type of lochia helps you catch postpartum bleeding or infection early. [learn more](GNS226_U1_T005#GNS226_U1_T005_h5)

question: Which of the following is an example of objective, professional nursing documentation?

options.A: Client is a difficult person who hates taking medications.
options.B: Client looks lazy and refuses to get out of bed.
options.C: Client cried during family visits and verbalized feeling hopeless.
options.D: Client is acting crazy and refusing to talk to anyone today.

explanation: Professional documentation records observable behaviors and direct client statements without personal judgment or bias. [learn more](GNS222_U3_T5#GNS222_U3_T5_h8)

question: A patient asks why women get more bladder infections than men. What is the best anatomical reason to give?

options.A: Your urethra is much shorter, which makes it easier for bacteria to reach the bladder.
options.B: Women have weaker pelvic floor muscles that trap bacteria near the urinary opening.
options.C: The female bladder produces fewer protective enzymes than the male bladder.
options.D: Your body temperature creates a warmer environment for bacteria to multiply.

explanation: You're building strong clinical instincts! Because the female tube is short, bacteria have a much shorter distance to travel to cause an infection. [learn more](GNS121_U2_T4#GNS121_U2_T4_h2)

question: A patient sits up on the side of the bed in preparation for walking and immediately reports feeling very dizzy and lightheaded. What is your best immediate action?

options.A: Lay the patient back down and postpone ambulation
options.B: Administer a strong pain medication immediately
options.C: Force them to stand up quickly to test their balance
options.D: Leave the room to fetch a wheelchair right away

explanation: Dizziness means the blood pressure has dropped too low upon sitting up, so returning them to a flat position keeps them safe from fainting. [learn more](GNS324_U6_T3#GNS324_U6_T3_h2)

question: Why must the objectives of an explanatory study be very specific?

options.A: To make sure no other nurse can ever replicate the study
options.B: To ensure the research paper is at least one hundred pages long
options.C: To prevent patients from asking questions about the study
options.D: To help the researcher stay focused on finding direct answers and proper statistics

explanation: Exactly! Specific objectives keep your study tightly focused on testing cause and effect without getting distracted. [learn more](GNS224_U1_T13#GNS224_U1_T13_h2)

question: What does a realistic healthcare plan take into account?

options.A: The personal hobbies of the hospital director
options.B: Architectural designs from foreign hospitals
options.C: International travel trends for medical tourists
options.D: Current staffing levels and available budget

explanation: A realistic plan matches its ambitions to what the facility can actually afford and staff right now. [learn more](GST321_U1_T7#GST321_U1_T7_h5)

question: Which joint do people sprain most often in everyday life?

options.A: Shoulder
options.B: Ankle
options.C: Elbow
options.D: Hip

explanation: Ankle sprains are super common! They usually happen when your foot rolls inward while walking or running on uneven ground. [learn more](GNS222_U1_T9#GNS222_U1_T9_h2)

question: Why do low-income households frequently purchase highly processed foods?

options.A: Government food programs forbid buying fresh produce
options.B: They provide cheap calories that quickly relieve hunger
options.C: They contain more vitamins than fresh vegetables
options.D: They spoil much slower than natural foods

explanation: Processed foods packed with sugar and fat are inexpensive and filling, making them an economical choice for families with tight budgets. [learn more](GNS227_U2_T020#GNS227_U2_T020_h2)

question: What is the main foundation of public health when looking at nutrition?

options.A: High-dose antibiotic use
options.B: Regular surgical screening
options.C: Adequate nutrition
options.D: Frequent vaccination

explanation: Great job! Eating proper food gives the body the energy it needs to stay healthy and fight off sickness, which is why it forms the bedrock of public health. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T13#GNS313_U2_T13_h1)

question: What is a very common cause of a large bowel obstruction?

options.A: Eating too much high-fiber food at one meal
options.B: A mild viral stomach flu causing diarrhea
options.C: An overgrowth of normal intestinal bacteria
options.D: Colorectal cancer or a twisted bowel loop

explanation: Correct! Tumors growing inside the colon or a loop of bowel twisting on itself (volvulus) are major physical reasons the large intestine gets blocked. [learn more](GNS213_U3_T9#GNS213_U3_T9_h7)

question: What type of language should a nurse use when documenting physical exam findings?

options.A: Vague and generalized terms like 'fine'
options.B: Subjective opinions about the patient's attitude
options.C: Clear, objective, and descriptive language
options.D: Complex poetic metaphors to describe wounds

explanation: Objective descriptions prevent confusion and provide clear facts for other healthcare providers. [learn more](GNS112_U6_T1#GNS112_U6_T1_h7)

question: Which nursing diagnosis is most appropriate for a patient suffering from constant urine leakage caused by a fistula?

options.A: Risk for infection
options.B: Ineffective airway clearance
options.C: Impaired physical mobility
options.D: Deficient fluid volume

explanation: Constant exposure to urine on the perineal skin creates a very high risk for localized skin breakdown and severe infection. [learn more](GNS312_U1_T16#GNS312_U1_T16_h5)

question: A patient is admitted with suspected celiac disease. Which specific blood test does the nurse expect the healthcare provider to order first?

options.A: Carcinoembryonic antigen (CEA)
options.B: Serum amylase and lipase levels
options.C: Anti-tissue transglutaminase (tTG) antibodies
options.D: Blood urea nitrogen and creatinine

explanation: Serologic antibody testing for anti-tTG is the standard primary screening tool used to detect celiac disease in clinical practice. [learn more](GNS213_U3_T8#GNS213_U3_T8_h6)

question: Which cultural factor often contributes to severe maternal health issues in rural areas?

options.A: Excessive use of modern antenatal care clinics in the first trimester
options.B: Reliance on unskilled traditional attendants for complicated deliveries
options.C: Early mandatory retirement for women of childbearing age
options.D: Over-consumption of iron-rich foods due to local cultural taboos

explanation: When women rely on birth attendants who cannot manage emergencies, getting specialized medical care is dangerously delayed. Community health education helps bridge this gap! [learn more](GNS226_U1_T015#GNS226_U1_T015_h5)

question: Which condition is a PET scan often used to help evaluate?

options.A: A simple hairline skull fracture
options.B: Bleeding right after a car crash
options.C: Alzheimer's disease and seizure focus points
options.D: Spinal pressure from a slipped disc

explanation: PET scans show changes in brain energy use, which helps doctors spot conditions like Alzheimer's or epilepsy. [learn more](GNS222_U3_T8#GNS222_U3_T8_h5)

question: Which bacteria is the most common culprit behind a bad case of strep throat?

options.A: Group A beta-hemolytic Streptococcus
options.B: Staphylococcus aureus
options.C: Streptococcus pneumoniae
options.D: Pseudomonas aeruginosa

explanation: Group A strep is the well-known troublemaker behind acute throat infections. Catching this early means doctors can prescribe antibiotics to prevent any nasty complications! [learn more](GNS311_U3_T6#GNS311_U3_T6_h3)

question: What is syndromic management of sexually transmitted infections?

options.A: Treating infections based on recognized groups of symptoms when lab tests are unavailable
options.B: Isolating infected patients in private hospital wards for weeks
options.C: Waiting for definitive blood culture results before starting any medication
options.D: Treating only the male partner in cases of recurrent vaginal discharge

explanation: Syndromic management allows prompt treatment of common STI symptoms during the initial clinic visit using standardized flowcharts. [learn more](GNS216_U1_T7#GNS216_U1_T7_h5)

question: What is the best position for a patient during an abdominal paracentesis?

options.A: Flat on the back in a supine position
options.B: In a steep Trendelenburg position
options.C: Lying completely flat on the stomach
options.D: Sitting upright or semi-Fowler's position

explanation: Sitting up lets gravity pull the fluid down to the lower belly, making it much easier and safer for the doctor to reach. [learn more](GNS221_U2_T19#GNS221_U2_T19_h4)

question: An older adult suddenly reports muffled hearing in one ear. What simple cause should you check for first?

options.A: A ruptured tympanic membrane from aging
options.B: Permanent damage to the auditory nerve
options.C: Impacted earwax blocking the canal
options.D: Degeneration of the cochlear hair cells

explanation: Always look for the simplest, most treatable cause first! A buildup of earwax (cerumen) is super common and easy to fix. [learn more](GNS324_U4_T7#GNS324_U4_T7_h2)

question: How can long-term fatigue lead to physical deconditioning?

options.A: Fatigue triggers the rapid breakdown of calcium in the long bones.
options.B: Exhaustion forces the heart muscle to beat at twice its normal speed constantly.
options.C: Lack of energy leads to inactivity, causing muscle weakness and reduced stamina.
options.D: Continuous resting stops the digestive tract from absorbing dietary proteins.

explanation: Makes sense, right? When you're too tired to move around, your muscles don't get used. Over time, they weaken, making everyday activities feel even harder. [learn more](GNS123_U3_T3#GNS123_U3_T3_h5)

question: A patient in anaphylactic shock gets an epinephrine shot, but after 10 minutes they are still wheezing and have low blood pressure. What is your next nursing action?

options.A: Discontinue oxygen therapy to calm the patient down
options.B: Wait another hour to see if the first dose takes effect
options.C: Give oral antihistamines instead of further injections
options.D: Administer a second dose of intramuscular epinephrine

explanation: Well done! If symptoms don't clear up, it is completely safe and necessary to give a repeat dose of epinephrine every 5 to 15 minutes while waiting for advanced help. [learn more](GNS221_U3_T12#GNS221_U3_T12_h6)

question: Bacterial vaginosis (BV) happens when there is an overgrowth of which specific organism?

options.A: Neisseria gonorrhoeae
options.B: Candida albicans
options.C: Trichomonas vaginalis
options.D: Gardnerella vaginalis

explanation: You got it! Gardnerella vaginalis and other anaerobic bacteria multiply too much in BV, pushing out our helpful flora. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T10#GNS216_U5_T10_h2)

question: What is your very first nursing action when a patient has an active front-of-the-nose nosebleed?

options.A: Instruct the patient to blow the nose gently to clear out old blood clots
options.B: Tilt the patient's head backward and pack both nostrils tightly with dry cotton
options.C: Lay the patient flat on their back and apply ice packs directly over the forehead
options.D: Have the patient sit upright and lean forward while pinching the soft part of the nose

explanation: You nailed it. Leaning forward stops blood from trickling down their throat, and pinching the soft part applies direct pressure to close off the bleeding vessels. [learn more](GNS311_U3_T5#GNS311_U3_T5_h4)

question: When pulling a cut interrupted suture out of the skin, which direction should the nurse pull the thread?

options.A: Away from the wound line
options.B: Straight down into the subcutaneous fat
options.C: In a fast circular motion
options.D: Toward the opposite side of the wound

explanation: Pulling the thread away from the incision prevents the exposed, germ-carrying part of the thread from dragging through the delicate healing tissue. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T12#GNS122_U2_T12_h5)

question: What is the highest possible score on a standard muscle strength testing scale?

options.A: Ten
options.B: One hundred
options.C: Three
options.D: Five

explanation: Muscle power is graded from 0 to 5. A score of 5 means the patient has normal strength and can push hard against your full resistance. [learn more](GNS222_U3_T2#GNS222_U3_T2_h5)

question: A 12-year-old child is brought to the clinic for repeatedly skipping school and running away. How should you as a nurse classify these actions?

options.A: Adult felonies
options.B: Violent offenses
options.C: Property offenses
options.D: Status offenses

explanation: Easy and clear! Skipping school and running away are classic status offenses because adults wouldn't face criminal charges for doing the exact same thing. [learn more](GNS225_U5_T4#GNS225_U5_T4_h3)

question: Why do unsafe injections carry a higher risk than many other medical exposures?

options.A: They always involve contaminated intravenous fluids
options.B: They cause immediate systemic allergic reactions
options.C: They are usually performed by untrained family members
options.D: They introduce pathogens directly past the body's skin barrier

explanation: Normally, our skin and mucous membranes act as strong shields against germs. An injection skips past that natural barrier, sending germs straight into tissue or blood. Brilliant logic to keep in mind! [learn more](GNS122_U4_T5#GNS122_U4_T5_h1)

question: A patient with a history of a previous heart attack is receiving counseling on diet and taking prescribed statins. Which level of prevention does this care represent?

options.A: Primary prevention
options.B: Tertiary prevention
options.C: Secondary prevention
options.D: Quaternary prevention

explanation: Secondary prevention focuses on early diagnosis, prompt medical treatment, and lifestyle changes to halt disease progression in someone who already has a condition. [learn more](GNS213_U1_T15#GNS213_U1_T15_h1)

question: A nurse wants to check birth and death rates in a district over the past five years. Where should she look first?

options.A: Interviews with children playing in the village square
options.B: Direct street observations during the afternoon rush
options.C: Existing government health records and vital statistics
options.D: A brand new questionnaire given to newborn babies

explanation: You got it! Birth and death records are historical government data, making them perfect secondary sources for vital statistics. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T18#GNS225_U2_T18_h5)

question: Why is it vital to educate family members about the fluid chart when they are visiting?

options.A: Family members must empty the bedpans during visiting hours
options.B: Education keeps visitors from drinking the patient's water
options.C: Visitors often give the patient drinks that need to be recorded
options.D: Visitors are legally required to sign off on the hospital chart

explanation: Family members frequently bring water, juice, or tea, and nurses must capture these amounts to keep the record accurate. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T19#GNS122_U1_T19_h8)

question: How do beta-hCG hormone levels usually behave in an ectopic pregnancy compared to a healthy one?

options.A: They rise much slower or fail to double at expected rates
options.B: They disappear completely from the bloodstream within hours
options.C: They double much faster than in any normal intrauterine pregnancy
options.D: They remain perfectly steady without any changes at all

explanation: Ectopic pregnancies often produce abnormal hormone patterns, failing to double as quickly as a healthy intrauterine pregnancy. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T29#GNS216_U5_T29_h5)

question: What is typically one of the earliest physical signs of significant blood loss?

options.A: Slow, deep breathing
options.B: Warm, flushed skin
options.C: High blood pressure
options.D: Fast heart rate

explanation: Tachycardia (fast heart rate) is the body's quick fix to keep blood moving when total volume starts to dip. You're mastering trauma basics! [learn more](GNS221_U3_T4#GNS221_U3_T4_h4)

question: Why must the money collected from selling drugs in a DRF be kept separate from other hospital money?

options.A: So it can be used exclusively to buy replacement drug stock
options.B: To allow the hospital director to take a cash bonus
options.C: To pay off old utility bills owed by the kitchen staff
options.D: So the government knows how much tax the pharmacy owes

explanation: Spot on! Keeping DRF cash strictly for buying new drugs stops the money from leaking into other expenses, which is how stockouts happen. [learn more](GNS223_U3_T8#GNS223_U3_T8_h1)

question: Which breath test checks for problems absorbing carbs or too much bacteria in the gut?

options.A: Pulmonary function test
options.B: Arterial blood gas test
options.C: Hydrogen breath test
options.D: Sputum culture test

explanation: A hydrogen breath test measures exhaled breath after drinking certain sugars to see how well the gut is handling them. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T10#GNS212_U1_T10_h5)

question: What is the main focus of 'andragogy'?

options.A: Managing hospital budgets
options.B: Educating pediatric patients
options.C: Teaching adult learners
options.D: Conducting laboratory research

explanation: Think of andragogy as the art and science of helping adults learn—people like you, who want to know the 'why' behind what they study! [learn more](GST321_U8_T2#GST321_U8_T2_h2)

question: What is the function of the flexible plastic canulas used in an MVA kit?

options.A: To seal the outside opening of the vagina during suction
options.B: To travel through the cervix and vacuum out uterine tissue
options.C: To measure the exact internal temperature of the uterus
options.D: To pump local anesthetic pain medicine into the cervix

explanation: Canulas are the sterile tubes inserted past the cervix into the uterus to channel the suctioned tissue into the syringe. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T010#GNS226_U5_T010_h3)

question: Why do we recommend asking open-ended questions when discussing a serious diagnosis?

options.A: It forces the patient to give a short yes or no answer
options.B: It allows the nurse to finish the conversation much faster
options.C: It prevents the patient from asking difficult questions about dying
options.D: It helps the nurse understand the patient's current knowledge and perspective

explanation: Open-ended questions invite patients to share their thoughts in their own words, showing us how much they truly understand about their health. Excellent communication skill! [learn more](GNS321_U4_T11#GNS321_U4_T11_h7)

question: In holistic palliative care, who is considered the 'unit of care'?

options.A: The patient and their family combined
options.B: Only the patient experiencing the symptoms
options.C: The attending physician and senior nurse
options.D: The immediate hospital nursing ward team

explanation: Think of it this way: an illness affects everyone in the household, so we care for both the patient and their loved ones as a team. [learn more](GNS321_U4_T4#GNS321_U4_T4_h2)

question: What are the tiny eggs of head lice that attach firmly to the hair shaft called?

options.A: Nits
options.B: Larvae
options.C: Spores
options.D: Pustules

explanation: Nits are the tiny, oval eggs that head lice cement securely onto individual strands of hair. [learn more](GNS112_U5_T5#GNS112_U5_T5_h5)

question: You are caring for a patient with severe preeclampsia. Which symptom needs your immediate attention?

options.A: An oral temperature of thirty-seven degrees Celsius
options.B: A sudden report of a severe headache and blurred vision
options.C: A slight increase in anxiety about the hospital stay
options.D: A mild increase in appetite during the afternoon shift

explanation: Headaches and blurry vision in preeclampsia mean the brain is under pressure and a seizure might be near. Quick action saves lives here! [learn more](GNS226_U2_T010#GNS226_U2_T010_h5)

question: Why does bruising often show up a day or two after a sprain?

options.A: Infection has set into the joint capsule causing skin discoloration
options.B: The body is reacting negatively to the prescribed pain medication
options.C: Excessive synovial fluid is pushing pigments to the skin surface
options.D: Blood leaks from injured small blood vessels into the surrounding soft tissue

explanation: When tiny blood vessels tear during a sprain, the blood seeps out and slowly travels toward the surface of the skin, creating that classic bruise. [learn more](GNS222_U1_T9#GNS222_U1_T9_h2)

question: Why must you split a 5ml medication dose into two separate injection sites for an adult?

options.A: Single adult IM sites should not exceed three milliliters
options.B: Thick oils prevent the plunger from moving past three milliliters
options.C: Patients are allergic to volumes greater than two milliliters
options.D: All syringes break if filled past the halfway mark

explanation: That's right! Putting more than 3ml into one muscle site causes too much pressure, severe pain, and poor drug absorption. Splitting it keeps your patient comfortable. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T3#GNS122_U1_T3_h3)

question: What is the main job of the mucus layer inside your gut?

options.A: To produce digestive enzymes that break down dietary fats
options.B: To absorb complex carbohydrates straight into your bloodstream
options.C: To speed up how fast waste moves through the colon
options.D: To trap bicarbonate and protect your stomach cells from harsh acid

explanation: Think of mucus as a protective shield! It holds bicarbonate right against your stomach lining to neutralize strong digestive acids so they don't harm your cells. [learn more](GNS213_U3_T10#GNS213_U3_T10_h1)

question: Why is keeping things strictly confidential vital for youth-friendly health services?

options.A: Government insurance schemes refuse to pay claims if patient names are published
options.B: Traditional leaders demand exclusive rights to review all clinic patient logs
options.C: Fear of social stigma and exposure will drive young people to seek unsafe, clandestine alternatives
options.D: Hospitals lack physical filing cabinets to store confidential adolescent records

explanation: Exactly! If young people are afraid their families or communities will find out, they'll stay away from clinics and risk unsafe options. Privacy saves lives! [learn more](GNS226_U5_T019#GNS226_U5_T019_h5)

question: What is the main characteristic of degenerative neurological disorders?

options.A: Gradual loss of nerve cell function
options.B: Sudden and rapid recovery
options.C: Temporary nerve inflammation
options.D: Infection of the spinal cord

explanation: These conditions involve a slow, ongoing breakdown of neurons over time rather than a sudden injury or short-term infection. [learn more](GNS222_U3_T15#GNS222_U3_T15_h1)

question: What is a major challenge health workers face when trying to eradicate disease reservoirs?

options.A: Poor coordination between human health and veterinary agencies
options.B: Immediate compliance from all community members during campaigns
options.C: Excessive funding that leads to unspent public health budgets
options.D: An overabundance of trained environmental health personnel

explanation: That's right! Controlling animal-borne diseases needs teamwork between doctors and veterinarians, but communication gaps can slow things down. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T6#GNS313_U2_T6_h7)

question: Why are confidentiality and safe spaces so vital when caring for survivors of violence in a hospital?

options.A: To encourage survivors to share their experiences without fear of stigma or retaliation
options.B: To hide the crime from law enforcement agencies
options.C: To ensure the hospital avoids paying taxes on patient care
options.D: To speed up the discharge process for the patient

explanation: You got it! Survivors are often terrified of exposure or payback. A safe, confidential space helps them build trust and speak out. [learn more](GNS312_U4_T14#GNS312_U4_T14_h6)

question: What is the main reason pregnant women get carpal tunnel syndrome in the third trimester?

options.A: A sudden tumor growth inside the carpal tunnel space
options.B: Permanent calcium deficiency destroying the bones of the wrist
options.C: Severe inflammation caused by repetitive typing work
options.D: Fluid retention causing tissue swelling that compresses the median nerve

explanation: Extra body fluid in late pregnancy swells the tissues inside the tight wrist space, pressing on the median nerve. Simple as that! [learn more](GNS121_U7_T6#GNS121_U7_T6_h5)

question: How do standard clinical guidelines across a health network help patients?

options.A: It guarantees consistent quality of care regardless of which facility the patient visits
options.B: It prevents patients from ever experiencing side effects from contraceptives
options.C: It allows nurses to perform major surgeries without physician supervision
options.D: It reduces the cost of prescription medications to zero for all citizens

explanation: Well done! Shared guidelines mean a patient gets the same safe, top-notch care whether they walk into a rural health post or a city hospital. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T019#GNS226_U5_T019_h2)

question: What does the Drug Control Act primarily regulate?

options.A: The cleaning schedules of hospital wards
options.B: The daily salaries of nursing personnel
options.C: The handling and distribution of controlled substances
options.D: The construction of public healthcare clinics

explanation: The act focuses on controlling how dangerous drugs are moved, made, and supplied in the country. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T13#GNS122_U1_T13_h2)

question: Why do bony spurs, or osteophytes, form around a joint with osteoarthritis?

options.A: Muscles pull too hard and stretch the bone outward
options.B: Infection causes new bone cells to multiply rapidly
options.C: Calcium supplements settle directly into the joint space
options.D: The body tries to spread out weight load after losing cartilage

explanation: As cartilage wears away and bone rubs on bone, the joint attempts to heal itself by growing bony spurs to help support the extra pressure. [learn more](GNS222_U1_T14#GNS222_U1_T14_h1)

question: Which screening tool is best for catching lung cancer early in high-risk people who don't have symptoms yet?

options.A: Magnetic resonance imaging of the brain
options.B: Standard routine sputum culture
options.C: Pulmonary spirometry test
options.D: Low-dose computed tomography scan

explanation: You've got this! A low-dose CT scan captures clear images of the lungs using very low radiation, making it the gold standard for high-risk screening. [learn more](GNS313_U3_T11#GNS313_U3_T11_h7)

question: A home health nurse observes that a family stores leftover prescription antibiotics on a low kitchen table. What is the most appropriate action?

options.A: Educate the family on safe medication storage out of a child's reach
options.B: Report the family to social services for child abuse immediately
options.C: Throw away all the family's food items from the kitchen table
options.D: Ignore it since the antibiotics belong to an older family member

explanation: Exactly! Medicines left within a child's reach pose a huge poisoning risk. Friendly education keeps everyone safe. [learn more](GNS324_U3_T11#GNS324_U3_T11_h7)

question: Which organelle is responsible for producing most of the cell's energy in the form of ATP?

options.A: Lysosome
options.B: Rough endoplasmic reticulum
options.C: Golgi apparatus
options.D: Mitochondria

explanation: Mitochondria convert nutrients into usable cellular energy (ATP), earning them the title of cellular powerhouses. [learn more](GNS111_U1_T5#GNS111_U1_T5_h3)

question: Which of these is NOT a good way to reduce waste in a hospital store?

options.A: Checking inventory expiration dates every month
options.B: Keeping storage rooms dry, clean, and out of direct sunlight
options.C: Rotating stock properly using FEFO
options.D: Ordering huge quantities far beyond what past data suggests

explanation: You got it! Over-ordering leads straight to expired stock and wasted money—definitely a practice to avoid! [learn more](GNS122_U3_T12#GNS122_U3_T12_h7)

question: Why must a nurse tape all tubing connections securely right after a chest tube is put in?

options.A: To increase the speed of fluid drainage into the collection chamber
options.B: To stop the patient from bending the tubing during sleep
options.C: To prevent the water in the seal chamber from evaporating away
options.D: To prevent accidental disconnection and a collapsed lung

explanation: Loose connections can let room air slip into the chest, which can quickly turn into a dangerous emergency. Always double-check your joints! [learn more](GNS213_U2_T15#GNS213_U2_T15_h4)

question: What is the main reason nurses ask patients to take off all jewelry and hairpins before an MRI?

options.A: To keep the changing rooms clean and organized
options.B: To prevent static electricity from building up on clothing
options.C: To stop the patient from losing valuables during the test
options.D: To prevent metal objects from turning into dangerous projectiles

explanation: Spot on! That giant magnet can pull loose metal items like a flying bullet, which could hurt someone or break the machine. [learn more](GNS222_U1_T7#GNS222_U1_T7_h4)

question: What is the term for the outward and cultural expression of a person's inner grief?

options.A: Melancholy
options.B: Bereavement
options.C: Mourning
options.D: Anticipation

explanation: Mourning refers to the visible customs and behaviors people use to show their grief publicly. [learn more](GNS321_U4_T8#GNS321_U4_T8_h1)

question: During a quick nursing assessment, which of these is an early warning sign that a patient is struggling to breathe?

options.A: Use of accessory muscles to breathe
options.B: Warm and dry skin on the extremities
options.C: A slow and irregular heart rate
options.D: Normal resting respiratory rate

explanation: Spot on! When breathing gets tough, patients start using their neck and shoulder muscles to help pull air in. [learn more](GNS213_U2_T1#GNS213_U2_T1_h7)

question: A nurse notices a patient's pulse oximeter reading drop suddenly from 98% to 82% while the patient is sleeping peacefully and breathing easily. What should the nurse do first?

options.A: Check the sensor position and ensure the patient has not slipped it off
options.B: Immediately start emergency mouth-to-mouth resuscitation
options.C: Call the doctor to declare a cardiac arrest code
options.D: Administer a stat dose of intravenous adrenaline

explanation: Sudden unrealistic drops without physical signs of distress usually point to a displaced sensor, loose cable, or motion artifact. [learn more](GNS212_U4_T6#GNS212_U4_T6_h8)

question: Why do nurses often mix pain meds with comfort measures like positioning and gentle massage?

options.A: Hospital policies strictly forbid using only drugs for post-operative patients
options.B: Non-pharmacological methods can completely replace the need for prescription painkillers
options.C: Medications work much slower if physical comfort measures are skipped
options.D: It targets pain through multiple pathways and reduces reliance on heavy medication doses

explanation: Combining approaches attacks pain from different angles. It helps patients feel better faster while keeping drug side effects as low as possible. [learn more](GNS123_U1_T1#GNS123_U1_T1_h5)

question: What is the most common correctable physical cause of male infertility?

options.A: Varicocele
options.B: Testicular torsion
options.C: Klinefelter syndrome
options.D: Cryptorchidism

explanation: A varicocele is an enlarged set of veins in the scrotum that doctors can surgically repair to help restore normal fertility. [learn more](GNS312_U1_T20#GNS312_U1_T20_h3)

question: Why might a patient agree with family planning advice at the clinic, but fail to practice it at home?

options.A: The medication expires too quickly
options.B: Bad weather during the journey
options.C: Fear of community or family pressure
options.D: Lack of clean clinic floors

explanation: Spot on! Patients often feel caught between great clinical advice and the heavy cultural expectations waiting back home. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T006#GNS226_U6_T006_h1)

question: When do doctors usually order a polysomnography (sleep study) for a sleep complaint?

options.A: For every patient presenting with simple sleep-onset insomnia
options.B: As a mandatory first step before taking a patient history
options.C: When a secondary sleep disorder like sleep apnea is suspected
options.D: To confirm the diagnosis of acute situational stress

explanation: Standard insomnia doesn't require a sleep study. We order polysomnography when we need to rule out other medical conditions like sleep apnea or restless legs. [learn more](GNS123_U3_T12#GNS123_U3_T12_h6)

question: Why is emotional and psychological support an important part of long-term care for pacemaker patients?

options.A: Emotional support prevents the pacemaker leads from coming loose in the heart
options.B: Mental stress directly drains the electrical battery inside the chest wall
options.C: Psychological counseling is legally required before every battery replacement
options.D: Patients often experience anxiety and fear regarding device failure or lifestyle limits

explanation: Living with a device in your chest can be scary. Being a supportive nurse means caring for their emotional worries just as much as their physical heart! [learn more](GNS321_U2_T9#GNS321_U2_T9_h8)

question: Why are beta-blockers commonly prescribed for structural heart conditions?

options.A: To dilate peripheral arteries and eliminate all body fat
options.B: To slow the heart rate and allow better ventricular filling time
options.C: To stimulate faster electrical firing from the sinus node
options.D: To thin the blood and stop all clot formation instantly

explanation: Slowing the heart down gives the ventricles more time to relax and fill up with blood, while also giving the tired heart muscle a bit of a break. [learn more](GNS213_U1_T5#GNS213_U1_T5_h8)

question: Why do patients with Addison's disease need to take higher doses of their steroid medication when they are sick or stressed?

options.A: The body normally increases cortisol output during stress, and these patients cannot produce their own.
options.B: Increased steroids prevent the kidneys from excreting too much sodium and water.
options.C: Higher doses of steroids are required to kill off invading bacteria during an infection.
options.D: Infection destroys oral medications faster in the stomach, requiring higher amounts to reach the blood.

explanation: Healthy bodies naturally make extra cortisol when fighting off illness. Since Addison's patients can't make their own backup supply, they must take extra pills to help their body cope safely. [learn more](GNS222_U2_T12#GNS222_U2_T12_h7)

question: When using Naegele's Rule to calculate an expected delivery date, what do you do to the months?

options.A: Subtract nine months
options.B: Add three months
options.C: Add six months
options.D: Subtract three months

explanation: You've got it! Naegele's Rule is simple: take the last period's first day, add 7 days, and subtract 3 months. Easy peasy! [learn more](GNS226_U2_T002#GNS226_U2_T002_h6)

question: How do community health nurses bridge the gap between workers and management?

options.A: By advocating for safe practices and helping design workable health policies
options.B: By taking over management duties and running the factory business
options.C: By hiding workplace injuries so the company looks good
options.D: By convincing workers to ignore safety rules to save money

explanation: Nurses act as advocates and educators, helping both sides understand that worker safety benefits everyone. [learn more](GNS225_U7_T8#GNS225_U7_T8_h8)

question: In which zone of the surgical suite are hospital staff still allowed to wear regular street clothes?

options.A: Unrestricted zone
options.B: Restricted zone
options.C: Sterile core zone
options.D: Semi-restricted zone

explanation: The unrestricted zone is the front area where you enter and receive patients before changing into your fresh theatre scrubs. Easy peasy! [learn more](GNS123_U5_T4#GNS123_U5_T4_h2)

question: A patient stops taking their prescribed tuberculosis medication because it makes them feel nauseated every morning. What kind of barrier does this represent?

options.A: Financial barrier
options.B: Language barrier
options.C: Transportation barrier
options.D: Side effect barrier

explanation: Adverse drug reactions such as nausea are common side effects that discourage patients from continuing their treatment unless managed properly. [learn more](GNS215_U4_T2#GNS215_U4_T2_h3)

question: Which emotional challenge often happens when older adults experience major life losses?

options.A: Excessive hyperactivity and euphoria
options.B: Depression and social isolation
options.C: Attention deficit hyperactivity disorder
options.D: Bipolar mood swings during sleep

explanation: Well done. Retiring, losing friends or family, and moving around less can make older adults feel lonely and lead to depression. [learn more](GNS321_U3_T4#GNS321_U3_T4_h3)

question: What is the key feature of a focal aware seizure?

options.A: The patient remains fully conscious during the event
options.B: Both hemispheres of the brain are involved simultaneously
options.C: The episode lasts for longer than thirty continuous minutes
options.D: The patient experiences a complete loss of motor function

explanation: In a focal aware seizure, the electrical activity stays in one area, and the patient stays awake and aware of what is happening. Keep up the great studying! [learn more](GNS222_U4_T9#GNS222_U4_T9_h3)

question: Which two nutrients are most important for keeping older adults' bones strong?

options.A: Vitamin C and iron
options.B: Sodium and potassium
options.C: Calcium and vitamin D
options.D: Vitamin A and zinc

explanation: Calcium is the building block for bones, and vitamin D is the helper vitamin that lets the gut absorb that calcium! [learn more](GNS222_U1_T24#GNS222_U1_T24_h8)

question: What do we call any sexual act forced upon someone against their will?

options.A: Psychological neglect
options.B: Sexual violence
options.C: Socio-cultural isolation
options.D: Domestic auditing

explanation: That's correct! Any non-consensual sexual contact or coercion is classified as sexual violence. Knowing these terms helps you advocate better for your patients. [learn more](GNS312_U4_T10#GNS312_U4_T10_h4)

question: What is the standard prescription cream applied from the neck down to treat scabies?

options.A: Hydrocortisone 1% ointment
options.B: Permethrin 5% cream
options.C: Clotrimazole antifungal lotion
options.D: Zinc oxide barrier paste

explanation: Permethrin 5% is our go-to weapon. Applied properly from the neck down, it safely wipes out both the mites and their eggs. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T97#GNS214_U1_T97_h6)

question: Why is it dangerous when communities keep quiet about adolescent sexual health?

options.A: It permanently stops physical growth and puberty changes
options.B: It encourages adolescents to seek out professional clinic advice early
options.C: It forces teenagers to rely on misinformed peers for guidance
options.D: It eliminates all forms of peer pressure in secondary schools

explanation: Spot on. When adults refuse to talk about these topics, teens don't stop wondering—they just ask their friends instead, leading to myths and risky choices. [learn more](GNS312_U3_T11#GNS312_U3_T11_h2)

question: In many poor communities, what is the main dietary cause of micronutrient deficiencies?

options.A: High intake of dairy products and fresh vegetables
options.B: Frequent eating of high-protein animal meals
options.C: Heavy reliance on a single starchy staple food
options.D: Excessive consumption of imported canned foods

explanation: Correct! Eating only one starchy food day in and day out means the body misses out on the wide variety of nutrients it needs. [learn more](GNS313_U3_T7#GNS313_U3_T7_h3)

question: A hospital board decides to build three new community health centers over the next four years. What type of objective does this represent?

options.A: Strategic objective
options.B: Individual performance objective
options.C: Daily shift objective
options.D: Operational objective

explanation: Long-term, multi-year plans involving major resource commitments are classic examples of strategic objectives. [learn more](GST321_U2_T3#GST321_U2_T3_h3)

question: Over time, why does high blood sugar cause damage to organs?

options.A: Sugar molecules directly injure delicate blood vessels and nerves
options.B: Glucose turns into a toxic acid inside major body organs
options.C: The pancreas stops producing all red blood cells
options.D: Extra sugar blocks the normal flow of oxygen to the lungs

explanation: When blood sugar stays high for too long, it acts almost like sandpaper on the tiny, delicate blood vessels and nerves all over the body. Spotting this early helps us protect our patients! [learn more](GNS313_U3_T3#GNS313_U3_T3_h1)

question: Using the ROME mnemonic (Respiratory Opposite, Metabolic Equal), how do pH and bicarbonate ($HCO_3^-$) move in a metabolic imbalance?

options.A: They move in opposite directions
options.B: They move in the same direction
options.C: They cancel each other out instantly
options.D: They remain completely unchanged

explanation: ROME helps us remember: in metabolic issues, the pH and bicarbonate are Equal (they move in the same direction—both go up or both go down). You've got this! [learn more](GNS121_U2_T13#GNS121_U2_T13_h7)

question: What is the sneaky trick that bacterial enzymes like beta-lactamase pull off?

options.A: They help bacteria digest human red blood cells
options.B: They destroy specific antibiotic medications
options.C: They speed up bacterial cell division
options.D: They create a thick capsule around the cell

explanation: Beta-lactamases are defense weapons for bacteria; they chop up the antibiotic before it can do its job. [learn more](GNS215_U6_T2#GNS215_U6_T2_h5)

question: What is the main purpose of regulatory oversight on generic and brand drugs in the country?

options.A: To ensure medications are safe, effective, and free from harmful counterfeits
options.B: To eliminate the need for nurses to check patient identification bands
options.C: To prevent foreign countries from exporting medical supplies to local hospitals
options.D: To make sure all pharmaceutical companies charge the exact same price

explanation: Agencies like NAFDAC protect the public by cracking down on fake or expired drugs, ensuring patients get real healing when they take their medications. [learn more](GNS125_U1_T8#GNS125_U1_T8_h5)

question: Which Nigerian agency is in charge of regulating drugs and keeping track of adverse drug reactions?

options.A: NMA
options.B: NAFDAC
options.C: NMCN
options.D: FMOH

explanation: NAFDAC handles the safety of food, drugs, and medical products across Nigeria, including tracking bad reactions. [learn more](GNS215_U2_T5#GNS215_U2_T5_h7)

question: What is a major source of crystalline silica dust exposure for workers in many Nigerian local communities?

options.A: Operating commercial transport buses in traffic
options.B: Fishing in coastal rivers and marine lagoons
options.C: Artisanal gold mining and stone quarrying

question: What must a nurse always do when a calculated safety box requirement results in a fractional number like 12.3 boxes?

question: Why do some women experience upset stomach or diarrhoea along with their menstrual cramps?

options.A: The uterus physically presses directly against the stomach and bowels

options.C: Prostaglandins enter the bloodstream and affect other body systems
options.D: Hormonal shifts cause a sudden increase in daily food poisoning rates

explanation: Exactly! Prostaglandins don't just stay in the uterus; when they travel through the bloodstream, they can also stimulate the digestive tract. [learn more](GNS216_U2_T6#GNS216_U2_T6_h2)

question: A patient is grieving because a stroke has taken away their physical independence. How would a nurse describe this type of loss?

options.A: Anticipatory mourning
options.B: Complicated grief
options.C: Perceived loss
options.D: Actual loss

explanation: Even though others might not physically see it, losing your independence is deeply felt by the patient. That's what makes it a perceived loss! [learn more](GNS221_U4_T6#GNS221_U4_T6_h1)

question: What is the main job of glucocorticoids (like cortisol) released by the middle layer of the adrenal cortex?

options.A: Managing stress and raising blood sugar levels
options.B: Triggering immediate fight-or-flight heart rate spikes
options.C: Controlling sodium and water retention in the kidneys
options.D: Stimulating the development of secondary sex traits

explanation: Cortisol is your body's main stress helper. When life gets tough physically or emotionally, it steps in to give you energy and raise your blood sugar to help you cope. [learn more](GNS222_U2_T12#GNS222_U2_T12_h1)

question: Which drug class is mainly used to calm down severe leprosy reactions and save nerves from permanent damage?

options.A: Antifungal agents
options.B: Broad-spectrum antibiotics
options.C: Corticosteroids
options.D: Non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drugs

question: Why do public health nurses and planners care about measuring disease incidence?
