options.D: It calculates the total hospital building costs needed

explanation: Spot-on! Watching new cases over time helps health teams know if prevention is working or if an epidemic is spreading. [learn more](GNS313_U1_T11#GNS313_U1_T11_h1)

question: Why is it important for you as a nurse to understand female reproductive anatomy?

options.A: To prescribe hormonal contraceptives without a doctor
options.B: To diagnose sexually transmitted infections by sight alone
options.C: To accurately assess health problems and provide patient care
options.D: To perform surgical procedures independently in the clinic

explanation: Spot on! Knowing your anatomy helps you spot when something isn't quite right, chat easily with your patients, and guide them through different stages of life with confidence. [learn more](GNS216_U2_T1#GNS216_U2_T1_h1)

question: A COVID-19 patient says they feel completely fine, but their pulse oximeter reads 88% on room air. What should you do first?

options.A: Wait for the patient to request oxygen before taking any action
options.B: Encourage the patient to drink more fluids and rest in bed
options.C: Discharge the patient home since they report feeling comfortable
options.D: Apply supplemental oxygen and notify the attending healthcare provider

explanation: Spot on! An 88% saturation is a red flag regardless of how good the patient feels. Always trust your machine and act fast to protect your patient. [learn more](GNS123_U4_T6#GNS123_U4_T6_h5)

question: Why do many patients prefer injections over oral medications?

options.A: Swallowing pills is physically impossible for most adults.
options.B: Injections are always cheaper than buying tablets from a pharmacy.
options.C: They believe injections work much faster and are stronger.
options.D: Government policies mandate injections for routine checkups.

explanation: A widespread cultural belief is that injected drugs enter the blood directly and provide a stronger, quicker cure than oral pills. [learn more](GNS122_U4_T6#GNS122_U4_T6_h2)

question: Which sign separates severe hyperemesis gravidarum from normal morning sickness?

options.A: Weight loss exceeding five percent of body weight
options.B: Mild fatigue during the afternoon hours
options.C: Queasiness that improves by the second trimester
options.D: Occasional dislike for the smell of coffee

explanation: Losing more than 5% of pre-pregnancy body weight tells us it's no longer regular morning sickness—it's hyperemesis and needs medical help! [learn more](GNS226_U2_T011#GNS226_U2_T011_h6)

question: What is the main purpose of placing a stent during a percutaneous coronary intervention?

options.A: To hold the narrowed artery open and maintain blood flow
options.B: To pump blood forward when the heart muscle stops working
options.C: To deliver strong antibiotics directly into the heart chambers
options.D: To completely replace the damaged coronary artery valve

explanation: A stent is a small wire mesh tube left inside the artery after balloon angioplasty to prevent the vessel from narrowing again. [learn more](GNS213_U1_T4#GNS213_U1_T4_h7)

question: What is the most common cause of hypothyroidism when iodine is readily available?

options.A: Hashimoto's thyroiditis
options.B: Anterior pituitary tumor
options.C: Dietary iodine deficiency
options.D: Chronic viral infection

explanation: Correct! Hashimoto's is an autoimmune condition where the body's immune system accidentally attacks and wears down the thyroid gland over time. [learn more](GNS222_U2_T10#GNS222_U2_T10_h2)

question: What does a drug overdose actually mean?

options.A: Taking two different drugs at the exact same time
options.B: Taking more than the recommended amount of a substance
options.C: Stopping a prescribed medication too suddenly
options.D: Experiencing a mild allergic reaction to a tablet

explanation: You've got this! An overdose simply happens when someone takes more of a drug than their body can safely handle and process at once. [learn more](GNS125_U2_T9#GNS125_U2_T9_h1)

question: A patient gets schistosomiasis after wading in a slow-moving stream. How did they catch it?

options.A: A bite from an aquatic insect vector
options.B: Water-contact with free-swimming larvae
options.C: Inhalation of steam near the water
options.D: Ingestion of undercooked river fish

explanation: Schistosoma parasites release tiny larvae into freshwater. If someone wades or bathes in that water, the larvae swim right up and penetrate their skin. Nature can be tricky! [learn more](GST114_U6_T3#GST114_U6_T3_h3)

question: Why do bedridden patients often need extra protein in their diet?

options.A: Bed rest causes the body to sweat out all available amino acids
options.B: Dietary protein replaces the need for physical therapy exercises
options.C: Illness and immobility trigger a state that breaks down muscle
options.D: Proteins are needed to lubricate the moving joints directly

explanation: Being stuck in bed puts the body in a breakdown state (catabolism) where muscle is lost faster. Extra protein helps fight off this muscle wasting! [learn more](GNS221_U1_T1#GNS221_U1_T1_h5)

question: Which type of nerve signals tell the bladder muscle to squeeze when it's time to pass urine?

options.A: Parasympathetic fibers
options.B: Sympathetic fibers
options.C: Enteric nerve fibers
options.D: Somatic sensory fibers

explanation: When you are ready to use the restroom, parasympathetic nerves from your lower spinal cord kick in to contract your bladder wall (the detrusor muscle) and let urine out. [learn more](GNS213_U4_T1#GNS213_U4_T1_h8)

question: What is the main body purpose of warning signs like pain and fever?

options.A: To act as warning signals indicating internal distress or disease
options.B: To punish the patient for eating unhealthy foods
options.C: To slow down normal blood circulation in the limbs
options.D: To increase the body weight of an infected person

explanation: Exactly! Think of pain and fever as the body's alarm system alerting you that something inside needs attention. [learn more](GNS215_U4_T4#GNS215_U4_T4_h6)

question: Why do we focus more on prevention than cure in MCH programs?

options.A: Preventive care stops complications before they become life-threatening
options.B: Curative care requires expensive machinery that is always unavailable
options.C: Curative care is prohibited in primary health care clinics
options.D: Preventive care completely eliminates the need for any medications

explanation: Spot-on! Stopping an illness before it takes root saves lives and energy compared to fighting an advanced disease later on. Prevention is your best tool as a nurse. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T43#GNS214_U1_T43_h1)

question: Which feature is unique to Crohn's disease when compared to ulcerative colitis?

options.A: It is caused directly by a specific bacterial infection
options.B: Damage is strictly limited to the inner lining of the colon
options.C: It features patchy 'skip lesions' and inflammation through all layers of the bowel wall
options.D: Inflammation is continuous and always starts from the rectum

explanation: Crohn's can affect the entire thickness of the bowel wall (transmural) and likes to leave healthy patches of tissue right next to diseased ones (skip lesions). [learn more](GNS213_U3_T10#GNS213_U3_T10_h3)

question: What is the specific name for Cushing's syndrome when it is caused by a tiny tumor in the pituitary gland making too much ACTH?

options.A: Cushing's disease
options.B: Conn's syndrome
options.C: Pheochromocytoma
options.D: Addison's disease

explanation: Here is a handy clinical tip: 'Cushing's syndrome' is any excess cortisol, but when the pituitary gland's tumor is the culprit, we specifically call it 'Cushing's disease'. [learn more](GNS222_U2_T12#GNS222_U2_T12_h4)

question: Which nursing intervention provides a simple, non-pharmacological method to relieve primary dysmenorrhea?

options.A: Administering intravenous broad-spectrum antibiotics
options.B: Placing the client in an absolute flat supine position
options.C: Encouraging immediate high-impact interval training
options.D: Applying local heat therapy to the lower abdomen

explanation: Heat relaxes uterine smooth muscle and helps reduce the ischemic pain associated with menstrual cramps. [learn more](GNS311_U1_T7#GNS311_U1_T7_h7)

question: What is the primary function of peristalsis in the oesophagus?

options.A: Absorbing water into the bloodstream
options.B: Moving swallowed food downward
options.C: Secreting strong digestive enzymes
options.D: Filtering bacteria from liquids

explanation: Peristalsis refers to the wave-like muscle contractions that push food along the digestive tract toward the stomach. [learn more](GNS213_U3_T5#GNS213_U3_T5_h1)

question: A young adult patient has lost a large amount of blood from a trauma, yet their blood pressure remains normal. What is the best explanation for this?

options.A: Young adults are immune to the effects of hypovolemic shock
options.B: The bleeding has completely stopped on its own
options.C: Strong blood vessel constriction is temporarily hiding the blood loss
options.D: The blood loss is minor and requires no further observation

explanation: Strong compensatory mechanisms in younger patients can keep blood pressure normal even after losing a dangerous amount of blood. [learn more](GNS112_U7_T2#GNS112_U7_T2_h3)

question: A patient after abdominal surgery tries to avoid taking deep breaths because it hurts. What complication are they most likely heading toward?

options.A: Atelectasis
options.B: Muscle contractures
options.C: Pressure ulcers
options.D: Renal failure

explanation: Well done! Shallow breathing stops the tiny air sacs (alveoli) from opening up fully, which can cause them to collapse and lead to atelectasis or pneumonia. Encouraging deep breaths is key! [learn more](GNS123_U5_T11#GNS123_U5_T11_h3)

question: A client with chronic kidney disease visits your clinic. Which nutrients must you watch very closely?

options.A: Dietary fiber alone
options.B: Simple sugars only
options.C: Sodium and potassium
options.D: Vitamin C and water

explanation: Brilliant! Diseased kidneys have a hard time balancing electrolytes, so keeping an eye on sodium and potassium is a lifesaver. [learn more](GNS227_U3_T002#GNS227_U3_T002_h3)

question: Which of these actions goes against safe infection control practice during venepuncture?

options.A: Recapping used needles using a two-handed technique

options.C: Performing hand hygiene before putting on clean gloves
options.D: Cleaning the insertion site in a circular outward motion

question: What does self-medication mean in everyday terms?

options.A: Participating in a clinical drug trial supervised by researchers
options.B: Using medicines to treat self-recognized symptoms without a prescription
options.C: Receiving intravenous medications exclusively inside a hospital ward
options.D: Taking drugs strictly prescribed and monitored by a licensed physician

question: What is the official paper form that Nigerian health workers use to report adverse drug reactions?

options.A: Blue Card Sheet
options.B: Yellow Form
options.C: Red Discharge Tag
options.D: Green Admission Book

explanation: Whenever you spot a nasty drug reaction in practice, grab the NAFDAC Yellow Form and report it! [learn more](GNS215_U2_T5#GNS215_U2_T5_h7)

question: Why is infection control a team duty for all healthcare workers?

options.A: Because cleaning supplies are distributed equally among departments
options.B: Because a single mistake by any staff member can put a patient at risk
options.C: Because only doctors are allowed to handle sterile equipment
options.D: Because hospital management requires daily written reports from nurses

explanation: Spot on! Keeping patients safe is a team effort. Because we all work together around the patient, one small slip by anyone can let germs spread—so every member's vigilance counts. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T2#GNS122_U2_T2_h1)

question: Why is a multidisciplinary team necessary when caring for a victim of breast ironing?

options.A: Hospitals require multiple signatures before prescribing simple painkillers
options.B: The patient needs medical, psychological, and social protection services
options.C: Physical wounds always heal faster when psychiatric drugs are given
options.D: Doctors are legally barred from treating burns without social workers

explanation: Recovery requires treating physical injuries, addressing emotional trauma, and ensuring long-term child safety. [learn more](GNS312_U1_T17#GNS312_U1_T17_h7)

question: Which of the following is NOT an ethical responsibility of the nurse regarding genetic test results?

options.A: Providing accurate and non-judgmental information
options.B: Respecting the autonomy of the patient in decision-making
options.C: Sharing the results openly with extended family members without consent
options.D: Maintaining strict patient confidentiality to prevent discrimination

question: Why must clinicians be very cautious when giving Class IC drugs to a patient with a history of a heart attack?

options.A: These drugs will immediately cause the patient's blood pressure to drop to zero
options.B: The damaged heart muscle will completely neutralize the drug within five minutes
options.C: Strong sodium blockade can provoke dangerous new arrhythmias in damaged heart tissue
options.D: Class IC medications only work when mixed with high doses of intravenous potassium

question: Why do patients recovering from severe heart trauma need continuous heart rhythm monitoring?

options.A: Rhythm strips are legally required to prove the surgery was successful.
options.B: Monitors are only used to calculate the exact daily calorie intake of the patient.
options.C: Damaged heart tissue can trigger dangerous irregular heart rhythms days after the injury.
options.D: The electrical system of the heart heals instantly and never causes issues later.

explanation: Bruised or repaired heart tissue is electrically irritable. Monitoring helps us catch dangerous rhythm changes early and keep our patient safe! [learn more](GNS213_U1_T9#GNS213_U1_T9_h8)

question: When is a doctor most likely to prescribe a drug like ranolazine?

options.A: When the patient has an extremely slow resting heart rate
options.B: When standard drugs fail to control chronic stable angina
options.C: When treating an acute emergency heart attack in the ER
options.D: When high blood pressure is the primary diagnosis to treat

explanation: Think of ranolazine as a trusty backup plan—it's usually brought in when the usual first-line medications aren't quite getting the job done on their own. [learn more](GNS223_U1_T4#GNS223_U1_T4_h5)

question: What is the golden rule of a therapeutic nurse-patient relationship?

options.A: Equal division of personal problem-solving
options.B: Casual, unstructured conversation style
options.C: Mutual sharing of personal life stories
options.D: Patient-centered focus

explanation: Correct! It's all about them, not us. We keep our personal wahala aside to focus on the patient's recovery. [learn more](GNS112_U3_T2#GNS112_U3_T2_h4)

question: How do free radicals and reactive oxygen species primarily damage our cells?

options.A: By stimulating excessive and uncontrollable cellular reproduction
options.B: By instantly freezing intracellular fluid and stopping circulation
options.C: By creating oxidative stress that harms DNA and cell membranes
options.D: By completely blocking the intake of dietary proteins

explanation: Free radicals love to steal electrons from nearby molecules. This creates oxidative stress, which can rough up essential parts of the cell like our DNA and protective membranes. [learn more](GNS215_U5_T3#GNS215_U5_T3_h4)

question: What is the primary indicator that the needle has successfully entered the lumen of the vein during insertion?

options.A: The surrounding skin turns pale and cold to the touch.
options.B: The patient reports a warm, soothing sensation in the hand.
options.C: A flashback of blood appears in the catheter hub chamber.
options.D: The tourniquet drops off the patient's arm automatically.

explanation: Blood entering the flash chamber confirms that the needle tip is inside the blood vessel before advancing the plastic cannula. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T16#GNS122_U1_T16_h5)

question: Within how many hours of a possible HIV exposure should Post-Exposure Prophylaxis (PEP) be started for the best results?

options.A: Within 72 hours
options.B: Within 1 week
options.C: Within 24 days
options.D: Within 48 weeks

explanation: Time matters! Starting PEP within 72 hours gives the best chance of preventing HIV after an exposure. [learn more](GNS312_U4_T13#GNS312_U4_T13_h4)

question: What is usually the main symptom of a small, uninfected vulval cyst?

options.A: No symptoms at all; it is often found during routine exams
options.B: Severe, throbbing pain that shoots down the legs
options.C: High fever and uncontrollable shivering chills
options.D: Continuous bleeding from the vaginal opening

explanation: Many small cysts don't hurt or cause any trouble at all. Patients usually only find out about them when a healthcare provider spots them during a routine checkup. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T7#GNS216_U5_T7_h3)

question: Which of these is NOT a typical complication of severe, untreated skin disorders?

options.A: Permanent structural damage to internal kidney tissue from skin flakes
options.B: Impairment of the skin's ability to regulate body temperature
options.C: Secondary bacterial skin infections like cellulitis or impetigo
options.D: Profound psychosocial distress and social anxiety

explanation: Spot on! Skin issues can cause local infections, temperature trouble, and emotional stress, but flaky skin alone won't damage your kidneys. [learn more](GNS213_U5_T6#GNS213_U5_T6_h8)

question: Why is it so important to set rehabilitation goals together with the patient?

options.A: Patients usually know more about pharmacology than doctors do
options.B: Hospital policies legally forbid nurses from writing goals alone
options.C: Goals matter more and motivate the patient when they reflect personal values
options.D: Collaborative goals take less time to write out in charts

explanation: When patients help choose their goals, they feel heard and stay much more motivated to work hard during therapy! [learn more](GNS123_U6_T2#GNS123_U6_T2_h4)

question: Why do doctors order an MRI or CT scan for a patient suspected of having GPI?

options.A: To check the exact amount of bacteria floating in the blood
options.B: To see how well the patient's body handles penicillin
options.C: To check for brain shrinkage and rule out other causes of dementia
options.D: To prove the patient has a brand-new skin sore from syphilis

explanation: You got it! Brain scans help us spot shrinkage (atrophy) and make sure the symptoms aren't coming from a stroke, tumor, or other memory issues. [learn more](GNS222_U4_T1#GNS222_U4_T1_h4)

question: A nurse organizes a stress-management workshop for workers facing imminent factory closures. What level of prevention is this?

options.A: Tertiary prevention
options.B: Primary prevention
options.C: Secondary prevention
options.D: Curative prevention

explanation: Spot on! Primary prevention focuses on stopping health problems before they start by promoting healthy coping strategies early on. Excellent! [learn more](GNS225_U5_T18#GNS225_U5_T18_h5)

question: What is the medical term for a deep bone infection that can happen if a bite goes all the way down to the bone?

options.A: Cellulitis
options.B: Tenosynovitis
options.C: Fasciitis
options.D: Osteomyelitis

explanation: Osteomyelitis means an infection has reached the bone and bone marrow. It's a serious complication we try to prevent with prompt wound care and antibiotics. [learn more](GNS221_U3_T11#GNS221_U3_T11_h6)

question: How do beta-blockers help a patient diagnosed with coronary artery disease?

options.A: By dissolving existing blood clots inside the narrowed arteries
options.B: By increasing the strength of every single heart contraction
options.C: By widening the peripheral blood vessels in the legs and arms
options.D: By slowing the heart rate and reducing the heart's oxygen demand

explanation: Beta-blockers block adrenaline effects on the heart, lowering heart rate and blood pressure so the heart muscle needs less oxygen. [learn more](GNS213_U1_T4#GNS213_U1_T4_h6)

question: Which of these is a common body trigger that can cause a seizure?

options.A: High iron levels
options.B: Excess vitamin C
options.C: Low blood sugar
options.D: Low dietary fiber

explanation: Correct! When blood sugar drops too low (hypoglycemia), brain cells are robbed of their fuel and can trigger a seizure. [learn more](GNS222_U4_T10#GNS222_U4_T10_h4)

question: What is a primary indication for prescribing central anticholinergic drugs?

options.A: Chronic high blood pressure
options.B: Bacterial respiratory infections
options.C: Elevated blood glucose levels
options.D: Parkinson's disease tremors

explanation: Central anticholinergics are frequently used to help control tremors and stiffness in Parkinson's disease. [learn more](GNS223_U6_T7#GNS223_U6_T7_h4)
